In an exothermic reaction, forming stronger bonds releases more energy than is needed to break the weaker reactant bonds.
Exothermicity indicates that the bonds formed are stronger overall than the bonds broken, not the reverse.
Exothermicity is directly related to the relative energies of bonds broken and bonds formed.
Exothermic reactions generally produce more stable products, rather than showing that the reactants are more stable.

The reaction is exothermic, but exothermic reactions have a negative enthalpy change.
